description:
AID-0050 (docs/ai-decisions/AID-0050-kvim-completion-smart-case.md), status Pending review.

Fixing the bd-8sh crash forced a case-matching policy choice, which is user-visible editor behaviour the maintainer would normally pick. Decision made without you: completion now uses nucleo::pattern::Atom with CaseMatching::Smart, so completion is SMART-CASE — all-lowercase prefix matches case-insensitively, any uppercase char makes the whole match case-sensitive. Same rule the kvim picker already uses.

Practical effect: typing 'Th' will no longer offer 'this'. If you want completion to stay case-blind, reversal is one argument (CaseMatching::Smart -> CaseMatching::Ignore in merge_and_rank) plus the merge_and_rank_is_smart_case test.

Alternatives weighed and why rejected are in the AID (prefix.to_lowercase(), CaseMatching::Ignore, CaseMatching::Respect, patching nucleo).
title: Review AID-0050: kvim completion is now smart-case (nucleo Atom)

description:
Found while wiring the GPU output head (bd-jrq). This is a CPU-path win, and it matters most exactly where there is NO GPU - Termux, which typically has no usable Vulkan driver.

THE PROBLEM. Neither SmolLM2 release ships a separate output.weight; both tie the output projection to token_embd.weight. crates/kopitiam-runtime/src/weights.rs loads token_embd through load_tensor_f32 - correctly, because the embedding lookup (gather_rows) needs real floats - and then the tied fallback does:

    let output_weight = match load_matmul_weight_opt(model, 'output.weight')? {
        Some(w) => w,
        None => token_embd.clone(),      // <- f32 clone
    };

So for every tied model - which is both of ours, and most small models - the SINGLE BIGGEST MATMUL IN THE NETWORK runs against a fully dequantized f32 weight. It skips the fused Tensor::quantized_matmul path that every other projection gets, purely as a side effect of sharing a tensor with the embedding table.

COST, SmolLM2-360M (49152 x 960):
  memory: 188MB of f32 held resident, where the Q8_0 source is 47MB. 4x.
  speed : the output projection measures 25-26ms per token on CPU, more than every other decode matmul combined.

WHAT TO DO. Load the output projection separately from the embedding table when they are tied: keep token_embd as f32 for gather_rows, and load a SECOND handle to the same tensor via load_matmul_weight (which preserves Q8_0 and takes the fused kernel). They are the same bytes on disk, so this costs one extra tensor handle, not a second copy of the data - and it should REDUCE peak memory, since the f32 expansion of a 49152-row table is the largest single allocation in the model.

Worth measuring both effects: tokens/sec on the CPU-only path, and RSS at model load. Expect the memory win to be the more dramatic one on a phone.

CAVEAT to check first: confirm gather_rows cannot read directly from a quantized tensor. If it can, the f32 expansion may be avoidable entirely rather than merely duplicated - which would be a bigger win again.

notes.author: fifad@Teddy-Thinkpad
notes.content:
FIXED. Bigger than expected, and it partly invalidates the GPU headline from bd-jrq - saying so here rather than letting the nicer number stand.

MEASURED, CPU-only path (--no-default-features, the Termux case):
                                  before     after
  'The capital of France is'       6.77s     1.39s    4.9x
  '...over the lazy'               7.03s     1.84s    3.8x
  token_embd resident            188.7MB    50.1MB    3.8x smaller
  weights load (gpu path)          570ms     418ms
Output byte-identical across cpu-only, gpu, and llama.cpp.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S OWN PLAN. It said to load a SECOND handle via load_matmul_weight while keeping the f32 one for gather_rows, and claimed that would reduce memory. That was WRONG - it would have held both the 188MB f32 AND the 50MB quantized, i.e. worse. The caveat at the bottom of the bead turned out to be the actual fix: make gather_rows read quantized tables directly.

WHAT LANDED:
1. Tensor::gather_rows now decodes ONLY the requested rows from a block-quantized table. A row is a whole number of blocks, so row r is exactly blocks_per_row consecutive blocks at r*blocks_per_row and decodes on its own. A forward pass reads one row per token - often one total during decode - so dequantizing all 49152 rows to get them was the whole waste. Refuses a straddling row or a strided/offset view rather than returning wrong rows.
2. ModelWeights::load takes token_embd through load_matmul_weight, so it stays Q8_0 where a fused kernel exists and still falls back to f32 where none does (the 1.7B's Q6_K). Win or no-op, never a regression. The tied output_weight clone now shares quantized storage instead of duplicating an f32 expansion.

HONEST CONSEQUENCE FOR bd-jrq: the GPU output head measured 4.9x against the OLD cpu path. Against the fixed one it is 1.39s vs 1.31s - about 6%. The GPU kernel is still correct, still tested, and still the right foundation for larger models and for prefill offload (3.9-5.9x, bd-2c2), but on THIS model fixing the CPU path mattered far more than offloading it. Anyone reading bd-jrq's numbers should read this too.

Gates: 156 tensor + 146 runtime + 70 ai green, clippy -D warnings clean in both feature states, aarch64-linux-android clean in both, netfetch canonical gate green on real weights.

title: runtime: tied output projection runs as dequantized f32 - 188MB and the fused kernel skipped

Part of the CJK / annotated-PDF field report (2026-08-01), epic bd-ski.
Original write-up: docs/issues/field-report-2026-08-01/

--- original GH body, verbatim ---


> Part of the **pdf2md CJK/annotated-PDF** work order — see the tracking issue for shared context, the corrections in §0, and the additive-corruption principle these cards rest on.

**Confidence:** Low (design). **Owns:** `apps/cli/src/main.rs`

## Problem

Facing five unfamiliar PDFs, there was no way to learn their shape without converting all five in full and reading them. `--pages` (shipped) helps once you know where to look; nothing helps you **find out where to look**.

## Change

Emit only the heading tree with page and line ranges — the `--index` content, without the body. Should cost a few dozen tokens against a document whose full conversion runs to thousands.

## Acceptance

- [ ] On a multi-heading fixture: output contains every heading, no body paragraph, page numbers matching `--index`.

**Depends on F-5**, or it faithfully reproduces garbage headings.
